## Flashcards

260 cards across 8 sets. [[PhilSci - Flashcards|Open the flashcards]] to study the whole course, one lecture, or any mix of lectures. Each lecture note also ends with its own set.

## Lecture notes

- **L01** [[PhilSci-L01 - Introduction and Logical Empiricism|Introduction and Logical Empiricism]] · 27 cards  
  *Historical roots of philosophy of science, Logical positivism and Vienna Circle, Rudolf Carnap on verification and metaphysics, Syntactic vs semantic conception of scientific theories*
- **L01b** [[PhilSci-L01b - Popper and Lakatos|Popper and Lakatos]] · 47 cards  
  *Popper on demarcation and falsifiability, Conjectures and refutations, The asymmetry of verification and falsification, Ad hoc rescue and the conventionalist stratagem, ...*
- **L02** [[PhilSci-L02 - Kuhn on Scientific Practice|Kuhn on Scientific Practice]] · 33 cards  
  *Thomas Kuhn and The Structure of Scientific Revolutions, Paradigms, normal science, and anomalies, Scientific revolutions and incommensurability, Helen Longino on values and objectivity in science*
- **L03** [[PhilSci-L03 - Under-determination|Under-determination]] · 28 cards  
  *Duhem's under-determination, Quine's Two Dogmas of Empiricism, The web of belief, Critiques of Quine (Stein, Laudan), ...*
- **L03b** [[PhilSci-L03b - GenAI, Writing and Philosophical Learning|GenAI, Writing and Philosophical Learning]] · 17 cards  
  *GenAI as a study aid versus a substitute for learning, Gartenberg et al. (2026) on AI in journal submissions and peer review, The institutional incentive diagnosis, Authorship, authenticity and responsibility, ...*
- **L04** [[PhilSci-L04 - Scientific Explanation and Understanding|Scientific Explanation and Understanding]] · 41 cards  
  *Hempel's deductive-nomological model, Inductive-statistical explanation, Asymmetry, irrelevance and correlation objections, Causal-mechanical explanation (Salmon), ...*
- **L05** [[PhilSci-L05 - Scientific Realism and its Critiques|Scientific Realism and its Critiques]] · 36 cards  
  *Metaphysical realism and idealism (Berkeley), Kant's noumena and phenomena, Eddington's two tables, Mach's radical empiricism and instrumentalism, ...*
